s1.syndrome_frame: Acute loss of consciousness with trauma and near-syncope episodes in an elderly patient with a history of hypertension
salient_findings: Episode of syncope with head and left shoulder pain
Near-fainting spells in the week prior to the index event
Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function
key_facts: Patient is in their 80s
History of hypertension controlled with Dyazide
Presented with 1 episode of syncope
Felt hot and light-headed before the syncopal event
Had a few near-fainting spells in the week prior to the index event
Vital signs were stable without considerable orthostatic changes
Serum electrolyte levels and cardiac enzymes were normal
Cranial CT showed no acute pathologic changes
Echocardiogram showed mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with preserved left ventricular systolic function
ECG showed sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block and fascicular block

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced syncope with preceding hot and light-headed feelings, consistent with vasovagal syncope

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of hypertension and presented with syncope, with ECG findings of right bundle-branch block and fascicular block, which could be related to cardiac sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: Atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's ECG showed PR interval of 204 milliseconds, indicating possible atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Sick sinus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's ECG showed sinus rhythm with right bundle-branch block and fascicular block, which could be related to sick sinus syndrome

shortlist.label: Orthostatic hypotension
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a few near-fainting spells in the week prior to the index event, which could be related to orthostatic hypotension

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including a PR interval of 204 milliseconds and later 210 milliseconds, indicate a first-degree atrioventricular (AV) block, which can cause syncope due to impaired cardiac conduction.

rejected.label: Vasovagal syncope
rejected.why: While the patient felt hot and light-headed before the syncopal event, the presence of structural heart disease and conduction abnormalities makes vasovagal syncope less likely.

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of cardiac sarcoidosis in the provided laboratory tests or imaging studies.

rejected.label: Sick sinus syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG shows a stable sinus rhythm, which does not support a diagnosis of sick sinus syndrome.

rejected.label: Orthostatic hypotension
rejected.why: The patient's vital signs were stable without considerable orthostatic changes in blood pressure and heart rate, making orthostatic hypotension unlikely.
